segments.text: Most people get this wrong. What's the real difference between a comet and an asteroid?
They're both leftovers from when the planets formed, four and a half billion years ago. But they're very different.
segments.headline: Leftovers from the beginning

segments.text: Asteroids are mostly rock and metal. Most live in the asteroid belt, between Mars and Jupiter.
segments.headline: Asteroids: rock and metal

segments.text: Comets are dirty snowballs. Ice, dust and rock, from the frozen edge of the solar system.
segments.headline: Comets: dirty snowballs

segments.text: When a comet nears the Sun, its ice turns straight to gas. It grows a glowing cloud, and tails millions of kilometers long.
Here's the strange part. A comet's tail always points away from the Sun, even when the comet is leaving.
segments.headline: Tails point away from the Sun

segments.text: That's because sunlight and the solar wind push the gas and dust outward.
segments.headline: Pushed by sunlight

segments.text: Asteroids don't grow tails. Well, usually. Some active asteroids leak dust, and some old comets have lost all their ice.
segments.headline: The line is blurry

segments.text: So the real difference is ice. Comets have lots of it. Asteroids mostly don't.
Tomorrow, pieces of both that actually landed on Earth. Some are older than Earth itself, and you can hold one. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
